description: Evaluation dataset for LLM translation of investor narratives to portfolio configurations

input.narrative: I'm Marcus, 28 years old, just started my career as a software engineer. I have $50,000 to invest and want to maximize long-term growth. I can tolerate high volatility since I won't need this money for 30+ years. I believe in technology and want concentrated exposure to tech stocks.

I'm Sarah, 58 years old, and planning to retire in 7 years. I have $500,000 saved and want stable income with capital preservation. I can't afford to lose more than 15% of my portfolio. I prefer US-based bond investments and don't want emerging market exposure.

I'm Elena, 38 years old, and I want to build a portfolio for my children's education fund. My kids are 2 and 5 years old, so I have about 18 years. I have $150,000 to invest with moderate risk tolerance. I'd like global diversification and reasonable risk-adjusted returns. No single position should exceed 15% of the portfolio.
I'm 25 and just started my career in tech like Marcus. I want aggressive growth and can handle volatility. I'm interested in tech stocks and have a 35-year horizon.
Similar to Sarah's situation - I'm 60 and retiring in 3 years. I need stable income and can't afford to lose money. Keep it safe with bonds.
Like Elena, I want a balanced portfolio for my kids' college fund in 15 years. Global diversification is important, and no single stock should exceed 10% of the portfolio.
Unlike Marcus's long-term approach, I'm a day trader interested in European markets. I want maximum returns and I'm comfortable with short selling.
Similar goals to Elena but I'm looking for steady 8% annual returns with minimal risk. I have a 10-year horizon and prefer US large-cap stocks.
Like Marcus, I'm young and want exposure to growth markets, but I prefer Asian markets for the next 20 years. I'm comfortable with moderate risk.
Unlike Elena's 18-year horizon, I'm saving for a house down payment in 5 years. I want growth but can't afford major losses. Maybe tech or large-cap?
Similar to Sarah but with a longer horizon - I'm a retiree who needs income from bonds. Very conservative, 10-year horizon.
Like Elena, I'm 40 with moderate risk tolerance. I want a globally diversified portfolio for retirement in 25 years. No position should be more than 15%.
Marcus-style aggressive investor interested in growth stocks. I want to maximize Sharpe ratio over a 15-year period.
Even more conservative than Sarah - small emergency fund for 2 years. Super safe, bonds only.
Taking Marcus's approach to the extreme - I'm building generational wealth over 40 years. High risk tolerance, want tech exposure.
Similar to Elena but more ambitious - I want 12% returns and am willing to take on significant risk. 8-year horizon, prefer US markets.
Conservative like Sarah but interested in European exposure with low risk for 12 years. Diversified, no shorts.
Professional trader unlike Marcus - I'm a hedge fund manager looking for arbitrage opportunities. Short selling is essential. Focus on tech stocks, 1-year horizon.
Elena-style balanced 60/40 portfolio for 20 years. Global diversification, max 20% in any position.
More conservative than Sarah - 5% target return with minimum risk. Conservative investor, 6 years.

rag_knowledge.content: Conservative investor, 58 years old, 7-year horizon, $500,000. Optimization: min_volatility, Universe: conservative, Risk: low.
Growth investor, 28 years old, 30-year horizon, $50,000. Optimization: max_sharpe, Universe: us_tech, Risk: high.
Balanced investor, 38 years old, 18-year horizon, $150,000, 15% max position. Optimization: max_sharpe, Universe: global_diversified, Risk: medium.
